title: Philosophia Reformata
author: Johann Daniel Mylius
epithet: A vast systematised compendium of the whole art
summary: Mylius's enormous digest of the alchemical authorities, laid out in order and illustrated with sixty emblems of the stages of the work — one of the most complete summae the tradition produced.

title: Viridarium Chymicum
author: Daniel Stolcius
epithet: A pleasure-garden of one hundred and seven emblems
summary: Stolcius's anthology reprints the finest emblems of Maier, Mylius and the Frankfurt printers as a single illustrated garden of the art, each plate under a Latin verse — the tradition's most compact picture-book.

title: Nicholas Flammel: His Exposition of the Hieroglyphicall Figures
author: attributed to Nicolas Flamel
epithet: The figures Flamel is said to have painted at the Innocents
summary: The English Flamel: a first-person account of a scrivener's alchemical enlightenment and a reading of the hieroglyphic figures he was said to have painted on an arch of the Cimetière des Innocents — the founding legend of French alchemy, whatever its true authorship.

title: The Art of Distillation
author: John French
epithet: The English laboratory manual of the spagyric art
summary: French's practical handbook of distillation and spagyric preparation, with figures of the furnaces and vessels — the working bench-side companion to the century's more visionary alchemy.

title: The Works of the Highly Experienced Chymist John Rudolph Glauber
author: Johann Rudolf Glauber
epithet: The furnaces and salts of a working chymist
summary: Glauber's collected chemical works in English — new furnaces, the preparation of his celebrated salt, and a practical, marketable chymistry standing squarely between alchemy and the coming science.

title: A Treatise of the Philosopher's Stone
author: Bernard of Trevisan
epithet: The nobleman who spent a fortune seeking the stone
summary: The much-reprinted treatise ascribed to Bernard of Trevisan, whose famous parable of the fountain and the king's bath became one of alchemy's stock allegories of the work.

title: Ripley Reviv'd
author: Eirenaeus Philalethes
epithet: A hidden adept's line-by-line reading of Ripley
summary: Philalethes's commentaries on George Ripley's poems — the most influential English alchemy of the age, written by the pseudonymous adept whom Newton and Boyle both took with deadly seriousness.

title: The Way to Bliss
author: Elias Ashmole (ed.)
epithet: Ashmole's prose treatise on the medicine of life
summary: The three-book treatise on the philosophers' medicine that Ashmole edited and printed to correct a pirated astrological version — his prose companion to the Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum.

title: A Golden and Blessed Casket of Nature's Marvels
author: Benedictus Figulus
query: Golden Blessed Casket Nature's Marvels Figulus
epithet: A Paracelsian anthology of the tinctures
summary: Figulus's gathering of short Paracelsian and Rosicrucian tracts on the tinctures and the universal medicine — a late-Renaissance casket of the chemical mysteries, later Englished by Waite.

title: The Last Will and Testament of Basil Valentine
author: Basil Valentine
epithet: The Benedictine's testament of the whole art
summary: The large English collection under Basil Valentine's name, gathering the mineral works and processes of the mysterious canon of Erfurt — the fullest testament of the Antimony author in English.
imprint: London: S. G. and B. G. for Edward Brewster, 1657

title: Aurora, or the Rising of the Sun (Paracelsus His Aurora)
author: attributed to Paracelsus
query: Paracelsus Aurora rising sun treasure treasures 1659
epithet: The dawn of the treasure of treasures
summary: The English 'Aurora' ascribed to Paracelsus, with the Treasure of Treasures — a visionary statement of the tincture and the universal medicine that shaped the Paracelsian revival in England.

title: A Choice Collection of Rare Chymical Secrets
author: Kenelm Digby
query: Choice Collection Rare Chymical Secrets Digby
epithet: The virtuoso's cabinet of receipts
summary: The posthumous cabinet of chemical and medical secrets of Sir Kenelm Digby — courtier, privateer and founding Fellow of the Royal Society — a virtuoso's ledger of the age's practical arcana.

title: A New Light of Alchymie
author: Michael Sendivogius
query: New Light of Alchymie Sendivogius French 1650
epithet: The Cosmopolite's aerial nitre, Englished
summary: The English New Light of Alchymie, carrying Sendivogius's doctrine of the hidden 'aerial nitre' that feeds all life — a book Newton read closely, bound here with a treatise of sulphur and the Dialogue of Mercury.
imprint: London: Richard Cotes for Thomas Williams, 1650

title: Idea Perfecta Philosophiae Hermeticae
author: Jean Collesson
epithet: A perfect idea of the Hermetic philosophy
summary: Collesson's compact statement of Hermetic first principles and the single matter of the stone — a short, much-copied French adept's treatise of the mature tradition.

title: Of Natural and Supernatural Things
author: Basil Valentine
query: Basil Valentine Of Natural and Supernatural Things
epithet: Minerals, spirits and the growth of metals
summary: The English treatise under Basil Valentine's name on natural and supernatural things — on the origin of minerals and the spirits at work in the earth, with the Twelve Keys often bound alongside.

title: Aurifontina Chymica
author: John Frederick Houpreght (ed.)
epithet: A golden fountain of English adept-tracts
summary: A late-seventeenth-century English collection of short alchemical works — Flamel, Trevisan, Ripley and others — printed by William Cooper, one of the anthologies through which the tradition reached its last readers.

title: Of the Nature of Things, Nine Books
author: Paracelsus
query: Paracelsus Of the Nature of Things Nine Books
epithet: Generation, growth and the homunculus
summary: The nine books on the nature of things ascribed to Paracelsus — on generation, growth, decay and the making of the homunculus — a cornerstone of the Paracelsian philosophy of nature, in English.
imprint: London: for the Company of Stationers, 1650

title: The Compound of Alchymy
author: George Ripley
query: Compound of Alchymy Ripley twelve gates
epithet: The twelve gates to the philosophers' stone
summary: Ripley's verse of the 'twelve gates' — the twelve operations of the work from calcination to projection — the most influential English alchemical poem, printed by Ralph Rabbards in 1591.
imprint: London: Thomas Orwin for Ralph Rabbards, 1591

title: Opera Mineralia
author: Isaac Hollandus
epithet: The Dutch adepts' work of Saturn and the stone
summary: The mineral and metallic works attributed to the Hollandus adepts — detailed operations on lead, antimony and the vegetable stone that were pored over by Paracelsian chymists across Europe.

title: Lives of Alchemystical Philosophers
author: Arthur Edward Waite
epithet: A biographical history of the English adepts
summary: Waite's biographical dictionary of the alchemists, with a bibliography of the literature — the Victorian gateway through which English readers met the whole cast of the Hermetic art.

title: Collectanea Chemica
author: Arthur Edward Waite (ed.)
epithet: A gathering of short English alchemical tracts
summary: Waite's collection of English alchemical treatises — Eirenaeus Philalethes, the Golden Calf, Bernard of Trevisan — a compact reader of the practical Hermetic literature.

title: Azoth, or the Star in the East
author: Arthur Edward Waite
query: Azoth or the Star in the East Waite
epithet: Waite's mystical reading of the Great Work
summary: Waite's meditation on spiritual alchemy as an allegory of the soul's regeneration — the psychological reading of the art in its most eloquent English dress.

title: The Marrow of Alchemy
author: Eirenaeus Philalethes
epithet: The hidden adept's alchemy in English verse
summary: The long alchemical poem under the Philalethes name, setting out the theory and practice of the stone in verse — English adept-lore at the height of the Interregnum enthusiasm.

title: Pyrotechny Asserted and Illustrated
author: George Starkey
epithet: The colonial chymist's defence of the fire-art
summary: Starkey's defence of chymistry as the true medicine — the New England-trained adept (and the man behind 'Philalethes') who taught Boyle and shaped the Hartlib circle's science.

title: Medicina Practica
author: William Salmon
epithet: A London empiric's practical chymical medicine
summary: Salmon's practical handbook of chymical medicine, appending English versions of Basil Valentine, Bacon and the philosophers' stone — popular Hermetic medicine for the London market.

title: Aphorismi Urbigerani
author: Baro Urbigerus
epithet: A hundred and one aphorisms on the stone
summary: Urbigerus's hundred and one aphorisms on the preparation of the philosophers' stone, with the 'Circulatum Minus' — a terse, much-studied English-printed manual of the mature art.

title: Archidoxes of Magic
author: Paracelsus
epithet: Paracelsian talismans and celestial medicine
summary: The English 'Archidoxes of Magic' ascribed to Paracelsus, on the making of talismans, seals and celestial medicines — a cornerstone of English astrological magic, translated by Robert Turner.

title: Five Treatises of the Philosophers Stone
author: various
query: Five Treatises of the Philosophers Stone
epithet: Five short English tracts on the great secret
summary: A gathering of five short English treatises on the philosophers' stone — including matter ascribed to John Dee's son Arthur — one of the little Interregnum collections of the practical art.

title: The Secret Book of Artephius
author: Artephius
epithet: The antimonial secret of a legendary adept
summary: The English 'Secret Book' of the legendary Artephius, on the antimonial water and the work of the stone — a short medieval classic long reprinted among the English adepts.

title: The Hermetick Triumph
author: Alexander Toussaint Limojon de Saint-Didier
epithet: The victorious stone, in an English rendering
summary: The English 'Hermetick Triumph', the victorious philosophical stone, with the 'Ancient War of the Knights' — a favourite late allegory of the art in the language of chivalry.

title: The Golden Tract Concerning the Stone of the Philosophers
author: anonymous
query: Golden Tract Concerning the Stone Philosophers
epithet: An anonymous adept's dream of the stone
summary: The anonymous 'Golden Tract', an allegorical dream-vision of an assembly of the philosophers debating the stone — one of the gems of the Hermetic Museum, in Waite's English.

title: The Origine of Formes and Qualities
author: Robert Boyle
query: Origine of Formes and Qualities Boyle
epithet: Boyle's corpuscular chymistry against the schools
summary: Boyle's corpuscular account of matter, laying the chymical groundwork that would supersede the alchemists' elements — the Sceptical Chymist's positive programme.

title: A Catalogue of Chymicall Books
author: William Cooper
epithet: The first English bibliography of alchemy
summary: Cooper's catalogue of the chymical books printed in English — the first bibliography of the subject, and a map of what the seventeenth-century English adept could actually read.

title: Aula Lucis, or the House of Light
author: Thomas Vaughan
epithet: Vaughan on the light and the first matter
summary: Vaughan's short Hermetic discourse on the 'house of light' and the universal spirit hidden in nature — the Welsh alchemist's mysticism of the world-soul.

title: Euphrates, or the Waters of the East
author: Thomas Vaughan
query: Euphrates Waters of the East Vaughan
epithet: Vaughan on the secret water of the wise
summary: Vaughan's late treatise on the 'water of the East', the mysterious first matter and universal spirit of the alchemists — the Welsh Hermetist's most cryptic English tract.

title: Secrets Reveal'd, or an Open Entrance to the Shut-Palace of the King
author: Eirenaeus Philalethes
query: Secrets Reveal'd Open Entrance Shut Palace King Philalethes
epithet: The most famous English adept-text, unveiled
summary: The English 'Secrets Reveal'd', the open entrance to the closed palace of the king — the clearest and most influential of the Philalethes tracts on the making of the stone, studied by Newton and Boyle.

title: Epistle upon the Mineral Fire
author: Johann Isaac Hollandus / Pontanus
epithet: The one secret fire the adepts concealed
summary: The short and celebrated 'Epistle of Pontanus', confessing the author's many failures until he found the single secret fire — one of the most quoted confessions in the alchemical literature.

title: Bloomfield's Blossoms
author: William Bloomfield
query: Bloomfield's Blossoms Camp of Philosophy Ashmole
epithet: A Tudor physician's alchemical dream-poem
summary: Bloomfield's verse 'Blossoms', or Camp of Philosophy — a Tudor dream-allegory of the alchemical work, preserved in Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum.

title: Fasciculus Chemicus
author: Arthur Dee
epithet: John Dee's son gathers the adepts
summary: Arthur Dee's anthology of choice alchemical sayings from the authorities, Englished by 'James Hasolle' (Elias Ashmole) — the collection compiled by the son of the great John Dee.

title: The Turba Philosophorum
author: Arthur Edward Waite (trans.)
epithet: The oldest debate of the sages, in English
summary: Waite's English translation of the Turba Philosophorum, the 'assembly of the philosophers' — the oldest and most venerable dialogue of the Latin alchemical tradition.
